checks: No eclipse at 1 of 34 covered epochs where the 1.19472 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 355917097 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.1947 days. The TESS mission detected a primary eclipse causing the star to dim by 1.32%, while no secondary eclipse was observed. The photometric signal achieved a high detection significance with a Box-Least-Squares signal-to-noise ratio of 449.9. Pixel-level image analysis using difference imaging confirmed the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 105.3, though the centroid showed an offset of 0.9 arcsec from the catalog position. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown system. The machine-learning screening score of 0.66 suggests a moderate likelihood that this represents a genuine eclipsing binary rather than an instrumental artifact or false positive.
